summary: Fayette County, PA steel Aermotor tower on Sugar Loaf mountain in Ohiopyle State Park, built 1921 and removed 1979 per sources; two online references conflict but confirm no standing tower.

facts.status_note: FFLOS says no longer standing; Forest Lookouts gives removal in 1979. A map landmark label and a video title still use the name; neither was confirmed to show a standing structure

access.note: Sugarloaf Knob, inside Ohiopyle State Park, is reached by a park road to just below the summit (Wikipedia). No source says the former tower site is open or what remains there

events.note: FFLOS: steel Aermotor tower built in 1921; 1921 newspaper calls it the new forest fire tower
Watchman on duty continuously at the new tower, living in a cabin at its foot; four-mile telephone extension to the tower
Watchman spotted smoke from a brush-heap fire some ten miles away; fire wardens located it quickly (newspaper item dated October 28, 1921)
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Forest Lookouts say the tower is gone (removed 1979). A map landmark label and a video title still use the name Sugarloaf Fire Tower. We could not read the video beyond its title and found nothing confirming a standing structure, so status stays gone and the conflict is flagged in the story.

sources.title: Exploring Historic Abandoned Sugarloaf Fire tower

notes_for_editor: Two agreeing sources (FFLOS, Forest Lookouts) on the 1921 build and no-longer-standing status; Forest Lookouts gives removal 1979, no detail. The 1921 newspaper item is quoted second-hand on Forest Lookouts. Brief kind 'tower' and elevation 890.9 m match FFLOS (891 m); no correction needed. The Pastmaps page gives Date Portrayed 2010 and Date Published 2010 (USGS topo), so the 2010 in the source title is supported. The landmark label and the YouTube title are the remaining conflicts: the label is on a 2010 map, and the video page text could not be read beyond its title. Neither shows a standing structure, and neither was checked on the ground; no site visit or park contact was made. Wikipedia's Sugarloaf Knob article does not mention the tower. The FFLOS page spells the park 'Ohopyle'; the story uses the park's usual spelling, Ohiopyle (Wikipedia).
